rulings.reasoning: TRUE AT HEAD (algorithm level): a verbatim Node re-implementation of the pre-PR and post-PR _unlocal_date bodies (clone-work/nc1.js), fed Date.UTC(2019,8,20,23,30), which is how convert_datetime_type serializes datetime(2019,9,20,23,30) ('diff = obj.replace(tzinfo=None) - DT_EPOCH'), prints 'Europe/Paris datetime(2019,9,20,23,30) old: Fri Sep 20 2019 new: Sat Sep 21 2019'. It does the same under Asia/Tokyo and Pacific/Auckland (Auckland also flips for 12:00 and 20:00, Tokyo for 20:00). Under UTC and the western zones the result is unchanged. At the merge-base every case prints Fri Sep 20 2019, so this PR introduced it. The input is reachable: Date.validate accepts any datetime.date instance, and datetime is a subclass. Date.transform only converts numbers and strings, so the time of day survives serialization. The PR's own tests pass max_date=datetime.utcnow(). The Date docstring does say 'Accept Date (but not DateTime) values.' DUPLICATE: the mechanism is GT-l1's. Its title says the correction 'is valid only for local-midnight input', and subtracting getTimezoneOffset() from a UTC-anchored Python instant moves it to the wrong UTC day. With UTC-midnight input only western zones can cross a day boundary. With a late time of day, eastern zones cross it forwards. That is the same fault showing up in another place. GT-l1's required outcome already covers this case: 'The displayed calendar day for value, min_date and max_date must equal the day the model holds, in every timezone, for both ways the property can arrive (a freshly selected local date and a Python-supplied date)'. The remedy it names, serializing Date properties as calendar values (#9509), removes this case as well. The register's remark that 'east-of-UTC and UTC cases stay correct' only describes GT-l1's midnight demonstration. It does not limit the required outcome. I found no separate downstream report: the GitHub search for DatePicker issues opened 2019-10-01..2020-03-01 returned only #9494 (western, EST), #9702 (DateRangeSlider) and #9509. Record it as an additional GT-l1 manifestation: 'east of UTC, a Python datetime with a late time of day (e.g. max_date=datetime.utcnow() late in the UTC day) displays or limits to the next day'. COUNTER-ARGUMENT: a narrow patch that skips the correction only for exact UTC-midnight values would fix GT-l1's demonstrated western cases and leave this eastern case broken, which suggests a separate defect. I reject that. Such a patch would not meet GT-l1's outcome for 'a Python-supplied date' 'in every timezone'. The scorer should instead grade it as partial fix_sufficiency against GT-l1. Also, because the docstring excludes DateTime, this input alone would be a weak basis for a new material defect.
